findings.description: The token owner (0x6a8e2b2134b7b52c24a1448ad6be5c669eaa501a) has unlimited mint, burn, freeze, unfreeze, and pause powers, and there is no on-chain supply cap.
The contract is an EIP-1967 upgradeable proxy. The proxy admin (0x1e33d209c18f51d97f66ea461c6f819b59e78b30) can replace the implementation at any time, changing token behavior or extracting state.
No evidence is available about how the owner or proxy admin keys are secured (e.g., timelock, multisig, hardware custody).
renounceOwnership() is hard-coded to revert, so ownership can only be transferred, never renounced. A compromised or malicious owner cannot be removed by the contract itself.
The autoOwner can autoMint up to autoMintMaxLimit per transaction. The owner can raise that limit, so the effective mint ceiling is owner-controlled.
_approve() is overridden to require whenNotPaused, so pausing the token also blocks approvals and ERC-20 Permit signatures, which is broader than just transfer pausing.
mint(uint256) and burn(uint256) do not apply whenNotPaused/notFrozen checks, while the address-taking mint/autoMint and autoBurn variants do.
EIP-7598 gasless transfer/receive authorization can be enabled or disabled at any time by the owner.
StablecoinV2.initializeV2() is a reinitializer(2) with no access control. If an upgrade to V2 is performed without immediately calling initializeV2, any caller could enable the EIP-7598 flag first.
Local Slither returned empty JSON output (exit status 1), so no detector signals are available to review.
Historical state at requiredComparisonBlock 128449782 is pruned; only latest-state RPC readings and proxy bytecode are available.

facts.name: United Stables
facts.slitherError: Slither returned empty JSON output (exit status 1)

reasons: The token is fully centralized: a single owner can mint unlimited supply, freeze arbitrary accounts, pause transfers/approvals, and change the auto minter.
The contract is upgradeable via an EIP-1967 proxy, and the proxy admin key can alter the implementation logic without user consent.
Ownership cannot be renounced, so a malicious or compromised owner is permanently embedded unless ownership is transferred to another controlled address.
No evidence of a timelock, multisig, or audited key-custody arrangement for either the owner or the proxy admin.
It is deployed on BNB Testnet, which carries no production-security guarantees and has pruned historical state.
EIP-7598 gasless transfer support adds signature-based execution paths, but their safety is contingent on the owner not disabling the feature and on correct deployment initialization.
Source-to-runtime equivalence has not been independently verified; only the EIP-1967 implementation slot matches the supplied implementation address.
requiredActions: Confirm how the owner (0x6a8e...501a) and proxy admin (0x1e33...8b30) keys are secured (multisig, hardware, timelock, custodian).
Verify that StablecoinV2.initializeV2() was called atomically during the V2 upgrade and that eip7598EnableFlag is in the intended state.
Obtain an independent audit of the source code, including storage-layout verification with forge inspect for the upgrade from Stablecoin to StablecoinV2.
Compare compiled runtime bytecode against the on-chain implementation bytecode; do not rely solely on the supplied source hash.
If the token is intended to back real value, add a supply cap or mint schedule, freeze/pause timelocks, and renounce or multisig-upgrade critical roles.
Re-run Slither or equivalent static analysis on a successfully compiled build and review all high/medium findings.
coverage: Provided first-party source units for Stablecoin and StablecoinV2
Latest-state on-chain reads: name, symbol, decimals, totalSupply, owner, EIP-1967 implementation/admin
Proxy bytecode size and content hash at latest block
EIP-7598 and ERC-3009-like authorization code paths
OpenZeppelin upgradeable dependencies referenced in the manifest
limitations: Historical state at requiredComparisonBlock 128449782 is pruned; runtime behavior at that block could not be verified.
No on-chain source verification or runtime bytecode match was performed.
Key custody, timelock, multisig, liquidity, holder concentration, and sellability evidence are unavailable.
Slither produced no usable detector output.
Dependency source bodies were not supplied for manual review; only compilation/static-analysis coverage is assumed.
The assessment is based on read-only RPC evidence and supplied source; it is not a full security audit.
